target_name: All-Obligation Netted Cheapness With Gross Profit
rationale: Substituting total liabilities for interest-bearing debt destroys the economic content the hypothesis claims — since (che − lt) is negative and lt-dominated for almost all firms, the "cheapness" leg becomes essentially a *low*-liabilities-to-price (i.e., anti-value, low-leverage) rank rather than a net-cash yield, making this both internally inconsistent with the stated hypothesis and a one-ingredient cosmetic edit of the archive's existing net-cash-times-gross-profit signal.

target_name: Net Cash Cheapness With Liability Coverage
rationale: Swapping the RMW-spanned gross-profitability leg for cash-flow coverage of liabilities is a genuinely diagnostic, economically motivated change to the archive's best performer that isolates whether the alpha comes from a profitability channel or a balance-sheet-safety channel, though the oancf requirement will cut coverage and any coverage decline should be checked before attributing changes to the mechanism.

target_name: Cheap And Not Raising Outside Capital
rationale: The financing leg is a near-direct restatement of the published net-external-financing / net-share-issuance anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Daniel-Titman, Pontiff-Woodgate), so the interaction is likely to be driven by an already-known standalone effect rather than by the claimed value-quality conditioning, and the proposal offers no test to separate the two.

High book-to-market interacted with weak operating cash flow is essentially Piotroski's high-BM × financial-strength result (and the well-documented value-premium-concentrated-among-non-distressed finding) with the sign reversed, and it is also largely the mirror image of Signal 2 in the same batch, so it adds little independent information.

Asset-composition as a conditioner on book-to-market is a distinct and untested channel here with high coverage and correctly applied industry ranks, but act/at is a coarse, heavily industry- and size-driven proxy that may end up restating asset tangibility rather than the reliability of book value, so the construction is plausible but thin.

target_name: Five-Year Cash Earnings To Enterprise Claims
rationale: Long-run normalized cash earnings scaled by enterprise value is close to the published enterprise-multiple anomaly (Loughran-Wellman) and to Anderson-Brooks-style multi-year earnings yield, and the stated claim that the denominator is "strictly positive by construction" is false — deep net-cash firms can have mcap + lt − che ≤ 0, producing sign-flipped outliers that WINSOR on the ratio will not cleanly fix.
